clue.text: Seeking the views of the directors?

definitions.text: Seeking the views of the directors?

parts.words: Seeking the views of the directors?
parts.note: sounding someone out is seeking their views, and a company's directors sit together as its board; together they name a person or group used to test ideas

explanation.definitionFit: A person or group on whom you try out ideas to gauge reaction is the phrase this describes.

clue.text: Superficial though striking party

parts.note: workers who are striking are out
a side is a party or faction in a dispute

explanation.surface: A party that looks impressive but has no depth.
explanation.definitionFit: Something superficial lies on the exterior only, not within.

clue.text: Farm animal requires a certain amount of routine attention

indicators.note: a certain amount of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Livestock on the farm need regular daily care.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'requires', but that is the link word between the farm animal and the hidden-word signal. NEAT is an old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an archaic word for an ox or cow, a bovine kept on farms.

clue.text: Sent in wrong direction, becomes very emotional

indicators.note: putting the words the wrong way about signals rearranging their letters

parts.note: E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Someone misdirected gets upset about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'direction' is a single compass point here, east, not a course of travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense feelings are deep and strong, so an intense person is highly emotional.

clue.text: The porter having a weapon upset celebrity

parts.note: a gat is slang for a gun

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: a big name is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A doorkeeper with a gun takes on a famous person.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns the celebrity word upside down. GAT is old American slang for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateman keeps the entrance, as a porter at a lodge does.

clue.text: Centre of front row is for a once-revered figure

indicators.note: the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter, here taken from front

parts.note: a din is a row, a loud noise

explanation.surface: Someone sitting mid front row in an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a line of seats but means a noisy row.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief Norse god was worshipped long ago and is revered no more.

clue.text: Duck in a roll-it would have been chicken at one time

definitions.text: it would have been chicken at one time

indicators.note: the duck is put in the roll, placing one inside the other

parts.note: a roster is a roll or list of names
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A duck tucked into a bread roll, though the bird was once a chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: A cockerel was a chick before it grew up, hence 'chicken at one time'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock bird starts life as a young chick, so it was once a chicken.

clue.text: Top man realising some reorganisation is called for

indicators.note: reorganisation asks for the letters of the preceding words to be arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A boss sees that his firm needs restructuring.
explanation.definitionFit: A supreme military commander is the highest-ranking officer of all.

clue.text: Members of a union having differences

definitions.text: Members of a union having differences

parts.words: Members of a union having differences
parts.note: a union here is a wedding, whose partners differ in race or faith, not a trade union of quarrelling workers

explanation.definitionFit: A wedding between people of different races or religions joins partners unlike each other.

clue.text: Remove superfluous weight

parts.note: something superfluous is extra, more than needed
ct is the abbreviation for carat, a weight for gems

explanation.surface: Advice to lose excess pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to pull something out, taking it away.

clue.text: Tear in to start living it up in the city

indicators.note: the tear is placed in the word to, inside it

parts.note: to rip is to tear

indicators.note: start asks for the opening letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Someone rushes into town to start having a wild time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' reads as a rush but means RIP; 'up in' just links to the definition. 'start' gives L and I from 'living it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital of Libya, a large city.

clue.text: Issue period returns

indicators.note: returns means the word for a period comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: a period is a span of time

explanation.surface: A periodical issue comes round again.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or give off, a verb sense of issue.

clue.text: Men go all out for the little man!

indicators.note: all out suggests the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A rallying cry for everyone to go all out to help a small man.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome is a small mythical being, a tiny man of folklore.

clue.text: Given a key to a beastly place, making complaint

parts.note: a sty is where pigs, beasts, are kept
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone handed the key to a pigsty grumbles about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a small infection on an eyelid, an ailment in the medical sense of complaint.

clue.text: Restriction put on a learner-driver and pedestrian

parts.note: a ban is a restriction
L is the learner-driver plate shown on British cars

explanation.surface: A rule binding a learner driver and someone on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pedestrian' looks like a walker but is the adjective meaning dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian writing is dull and uninspired, as is something trite.

clue.text: Like a bird that's not in the least colourful

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
a hen is a bird

explanation.surface: A drab bird compared with a more colourful one.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashen face is pale grey, quite without colour.

clue.text: Mean article few agree about

annotationWithheld.why: 'Mean article few agree about' (7): A (article) leaves VERAGE, an anagram of AGREE plus V, and nothing in the clue as held gives V unless 'few' is a misread (perhaps 'five'); no scan or search confirms it

clue.text: No sound form of medication

parts.note: to strum is to sound the strings of a guitar

explanation.surface: Some kind of medicine that makes no noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack remedy, a medicine of doubtful worth.

clue.text: Flash but popular and virtuous person-a hard worker

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
ST abbreviates saint, a virtuous person
ants are proverbially industrious

explanation.surface: A showy yet upright person who works hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' looks like the adjective for showy but is the noun for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant is a moment, as brief as a flash.

clue.text: Held in contempt and cut without point

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the cut goes round the point

parts.note: to score is to cut lines into a surface
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone despised and cut off with no point made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorned means treated with disdain and disrespect.

clue.text: Storm when English politician got involved in trial

indicators.note: got involved in places the earlier words inside the trial

parts.note: a test is a trial or examination
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Uproar when an English MP is caught up in a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm.

clue.text: Underwear for a woman painter

definitions.meaning: a woman's close-fitting undergarment or vest once called by this name
Sir Stanley, the English painter of Cookham

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a woman's undervest and the English artist Stanley of Cookham fame.

clue.text: Guards possibly effecting rescues

indicators.note: possibly effecting suggests the letters might be worked into a different word

explanation.surface: Guards may be carrying out rescues.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure something is to make it safe, guarding it from harm.

clue.text: A poet's bloomer

definitions.meaning: Thomas, the Elizabethan poet and composer
a pink or white wild flower, something that blooms

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to both the poet Thomas and a wild flower of the pink family.

clue.text: See post is dealt with

indicators.note: dealt with suggests the letters are handled and redistributed like cards

explanation.surface: Seeing that the mail has been handled.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to see or notice it.

clue.text: A scholar turning to ice getting a cloak

indicators.note: turning means the scholar's letters are turned round to read backwards

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar

explanation.surface: An academic turning to ice gets a cloak to keep warm.
explanation.definitionFit: An amice is a cloak or a white linen vestment worn by priests.

clue.text: Soldiers in denim-pioneers

indicators.note: in says the soldiers are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Soldiers wearing denim are trailblazers.
explanation.walkthrough: An IMPI is a Zulu regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a body of Zulu warriors.

clue.text: Get together for tea?

definitions.meaning: to pair up or couple, as animals do
a South American herbal brew from holly leaves

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to pair off and also names the South American infusion drunk from a gourd.

clue.text: A report of ever-increasing trade

definitions.meaning: a loud bang, as of a gun going off
a time of rapid business growth

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a deep loud sound and a period of rapid economic expansion.

clue.text: The authority to give a fellow time

parts.note: a man is a fellow
a date is a time

explanation.surface: Permission to give a man an appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is official authority granted to act.

clue.text: Establishing a radical system

definitions.meaning: radical in its literal sense of relating to roots, so the network of a plant's roots

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both firmly settling something and a plant's network of roots.

clue.text: Coming about new meter is good publicity

indicators.note: about means the coming goes round the other letters

parts.note: advent means a coming or arrival

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An arrival of a new gas meter is publicised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the letters of METER IS to RTISEME, which ADVENT goes 'about'; 'Coming' looks like a verb but is the noun for arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: An advertisement is a public notice promoting something, publicity for it.
